reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in distinguishing causal impact from mere correlation. Supervised learning focuses on minimizing prediction error, which does not equate to identifying true counterfactual effects. The fundamental problem of causal inference arises when we observe outcomes but cannot determine what would have happened under alternative treatments—such as a defender not making a tackle. This necessitates explicit modeling of counterfactuals, where the difference in expected outcomes with and without intervention defines the causal effect. Traditional metrics like residuals fail because they reflect prediction failures rather than causal contributions. To address this, the framework employs multi-agent transformers to model simultaneous player interactions and uses propensity scoring to balance treatment and control groups, ensuring apples-to-apples comparisons. The validation process includes sensitivity analysis via Rosenbaum bounds and E-values to assess robustness against hidden biases. These methods together enable precise estimation of Expected Points Saved (EPS) per tackle, capturing genuine defensive value beyond surface-level statistics.
